hook_text: SPST, SPDT, DPDT. Alphabet soup until you count two things.
clip_script: A switch is metal that touches or does not. Count poles: how many circuits at once. Count throws: how many places each can connect to. Push-to-make: on while pressed, springs back. Doorbell, test button. SPST: plain on-off, two terminals, stays put. Light switch, your buzzer silence switch. SPDT: one wire to either of two, three terminals. This lamp or that lamp. DPDT: two wires each to either of two, six terminals, one lever. Cross the wires and a motor reverses. Choosing one: how many circuits, how many positions, stay or spring, how many amps. And always draw it open.
visual_style: Whiteboard contacts opening and closing; terminal counts 2, 3, 6 under three switches; a motor with crossed wires flipping direction; a checklist of four questions.
mood: Brisk and tidy, like sorting a drawer.
pacing: Touch or not, poles, throws, push, SPST, SPDT, DPDT, reverse, choose, draw open.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count the terminals on three switches at home.
